segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: We are here today to discuss the U.S.-China relationship and the investments that we need to keep our nation secure, competitive, and strong and maintain our leadership on the world stage. And let me make clear from the outset, when we talk about competing against China and countering Chinese influence,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: we're talking about competing against its government, not the Chinese people or the millions of Chinese Americans who helped make our country
great.
I'm

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: glad to have Secretaries Austin, Blinken, and Raimondo here to discuss the all-of-government approach we need to meet this challenge. And as this is

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: our first full committee hearing, I do want to thank Vice Chair Collins, as well as our Chairs and Ranking Members Tester, Coons, Shaheen, Graham, and Moran for working with us on this topic that I know every one of our members cares about.
And

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: I'd like to thank all of my colleagues for their work in the recent weeks to jumpstart our appropriations process and hold more than 30 very substantive hearings on President Biden's

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: budget request and critical issues. We have made important progress, but I hope we can keep things on track and mark up our bills soon. Vice Chair Collins and I had

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: hoped that this Thursday would be our first full committee markup.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: She and I are working very hard and will update all of our committee members on when we expect to have our first markup in the June work period. This week in the House, they are getting ready to mark up their own appropriations bills. It is my goal, and I know the goal of Senator Collins, to be marking up in a similar timeframe. What every member in this room knows, too, is that the Senate must have its voice heard in this process.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: To that end, this committee has received critical input from nearly all 100 senators to inform our work as we craft our spending bills that meet our nation's needs. We owe it to our colleagues and our communities, and most of all, our constituents, to put forward the shared priorities of this chamber in a slate of bipartisan spending bills. And this hearing offers a valuable opportunity to go in-depth

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: on one of those shared priorities, making the
investment

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: that our nation needs to stay ahead of the Chinese government and other competitors who are doing

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: everything they can to try and overtake America

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: economically, militarily, and on the world stage. As I have said throughout our

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: subcommittee hearings, keeping our country safe and competitive is not just about defense spending. Keeping our country safe means investing in diplomacy and

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: development to counter political and economic coercion
and
to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: promote stability, to stand up to autocrats, to support our allies, and advance our global leadership instead of ceding ground to the governments of China and Russia. Keeping our communities safe means funding to stop deadly fentanyl from crossing our borders, and dangerous cyber attacks that can decimate our infrastructure, our schools, our hospitals, and

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: more. And it means funding to make sure our supply chains

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: for drugs, food, baby formula, and more are safe, are

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: stable, and not dependent on the whims of Beijing and
others. And

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: when it comes to keeping our competitive edge on the world stage, that means investing in American innovation with funding for R&D, advanced manufacturing like we passed in the Chips and Science Act, clean energy jobs, cutting-edge biomedical research, emerging technologies like AI, and more.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: It means investing in our economy at every level, supporting our farmers

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: and small businesses, maintaining our ports and our railways, and other infrastructure that we need for trade, strengthening

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00
segments.text: and expanding our trade partnerships so we can sell American goods across the world, protecting our intellectual property, and of course, we cannot be competitive with the Chinese government if we are not investing in the backbone of

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: our economy, our working families.
We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: cannot compete without investing in high-quality public schools for our kids. We cannot

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: compete without investing in higher education and workforce programs that help key industries find the workers that they need. And we're stunning the efforts

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: to rebuild American manufacturing and so many other sectors of our economy if we refuse to

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: tackle the childcare crisis that is keeping parents out of the workforce.
And

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: not only are these issues as important as our defense investments, they are connected. Make no mistake,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: China is pressing forward with an aggressive modernization and expansion

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: of their military capabilities. As such, there are certain investments we absolutely must make to strengthen our own defensive and deterrence capabilities. The President's budget requests the largest ever amount of funding for the Pacific Deterrence Initiative, and that is critical.
We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: need to ensure the military has the resources it needs to stay ahead of China's military modernization,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: strengthen logistical preparedness, and expand cyber capabilities and more. However, as the

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Secretary of Defense has said repeatedly, keeping our nation safe requires a whole-of-government approach. After all, our weapons need chips.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: So making them ourselves and working with like-minded

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: partners to secure our supply chains is a matter of national security. And this is key. We need to make sure we have a regular appropriations process so every department, including DOD, can plan for the year ahead. We cannot settle for CRs that

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: freeze our progress.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: result in year-over-year funding cuts, and seriously impair every single one of our agency's abilities to fulfill their missions and move our country forward. The Chinese Communist Party doesn't

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: govern by CRs, and they don't govern by cuts, and we can't either.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: Which is why it's been so important to me, and I know Senator Collins and many others, to make sure we meet this moment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_01
segments.text: do our jobs,

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: and get our bipartisan funding bills passed in a timely way. I'm glad to say we have bipartisan agreement on the problem we are here to discuss today: keeping ahead of the Chinese government and our competitors. And based on our past bipartisan efforts, I think we do have a shared understanding that the solution here must be an all-of-government approach.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Just a few months ago, we passed an appropriations bill for this fiscal year that showed Congress can take this challenge seriously. Senators Shaheen and Moran worked

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: together to increase funding for the National Science Foundation and fund the Tech Hubs Program, building on our Bipartisan Chips and Science Act to invest in R&D and innovation and building a strong STEM

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: workforce.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: Senator Coons and Graham secured additional resources to advance U.S. global leadership by growing our diplomatic footprint, especially in the Indo-Pacific, increasing funding for the Indo-Pacific strategy, and providing

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: funding and flexibility for agencies like State, USAID, and the Development Finance Corporation to address emerging strategic priorities.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Senators Murphy and Capito made critical funding increases to improve detection and seizure of narcotics like fentanyl and related illicit contraband, and to dismantle and disrupt transnational criminal organizations.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: Senators Feinstein and Kennedy worked together to increase funding for the Office of Science and Department

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: at the Department of Energy and fund our national labs so we can develop clean energy solutions and improve advanced manufacturing. Our funding bill and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law also included critical investments to support infrastructure improvements to ensure our ports can ship goods around the world.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: I think it's safe to say we showed just a few months ago there is bipartisan support for an across-the-board effort to counter the growing influence of China's Communist Party. But if we want to stay competitive, if we want to stay ahead, we have to stay the course and build on those investments, which is why I find the approach House Republicans have called for dangerous, suggesting massive funding cuts across the government at a pivotal moment.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: After years of bipartisan consensus

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: for maintaining America's global leadership, that tactic will throw in the towel to our competitors and give the Chinese government our spot as

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: the global superpower of the 21st century. Because, let's be clear, House Republicans aren't just proposing one year of cuts to R&D and diplomacy and workforce programs. Essentially, everything that keeps us competitive.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: They are demanding spending caps that will tie our hands and lock in even more cuts over the next decade. I worry that what is being proposed leads to a lost decade for America in a moment when we cannot afford it. So let's be clear, China is not debating whether to pay its debts or wreck its economy. China is not debating whether

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: to invest in its future or cut and cap the investments that keep it competitive.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: and China does not operate on CRs. The more we play with default and punt investments and teeter on the edge of government shutdowns, the more we prove China and our competitors are right in helping them show the world that it is their moment to overshadow our leadership, and helping them demonstrate their core belief that totalitarianism is stronger than democratic values here at home and around the world. That is why it is so critical for the Senate to make its voice

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: heard on America's future.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: We have to show that there is a bipartisan vision to strengthen our nation's competitiveness and security by investing

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: in American leadership across the board and a bipartisan will to get it done. That is why I've been focused in all of our subcommittee hearings. It's what I hope to hear

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: about from our witnesses today, and it's why I want all of us to continue our work and mark up bipartisan spending bills soon. Because the bottom line,
We

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_02
segments.text: find ourselves today at a real turning point, and this year's government spending bills will determine whether or not we are prepared to compete with China and whether or

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: not we will stay ahead or fall behind. We cannot close our eyes or plug
our ears

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: when it comes to the threat the Chinese government poses. We have got to build on the progress we've made, keep our country safe and competitive, and invest in America's future.
As we

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_06
segments.text: decide what investments we do or don't make, the stakes couldn't be higher and they could not be more serious. So I want to thank everyone who's here today. Thank our witnesses. We
look

segments.speaker: SPEAKER_03
segments.text: forward to hearing your testimony today. And I will turn it over to Vice Chair Collins for her opening statement.
